lead.headline: Vermont logged 77 private-sale gun background checks in 2022: 0.17 per 100 dealer checks, last of 10 states requiring them
lead.number: 0.17 private-sale checks per 100 dealer checks; median of the 10 law states 2.2; median of states with no law 0.10
lead.watch_out: The dealer picks the "private sale" code, so this may show how Vermont sales get logged, not that sellers skip the check; the table stops at Sep 2023.

But do we know that some private sellers were already going to licensed dealers even before the law was passed because they wanted to know they were selling their guns to someone legally allowed to have one. The report shows a spike after the law was passed. In 2017, Vermont-based gun shops submitted 48 private sales background checks to the FBI's database. As of Oct. 31, 2018, they had submitted 90. That's about double the previous year. Other than firearms dealers, there isn't another option for people who want to do private sales to get the background checks required by law.
